thread:
jordan (support): FYI — Acme security just opened an escalation. They claim the keystore API is returning key IDs in plaintext in some error paths and their scanner flagged it as CVE-2026-XXXX. They want an ETA to patch and an immediate mitigation + key rotation plan. Attaching their repro below.

frank (Acme-Sec): repro steps: curl to our test tenant shows leaked key ids in /v1/keystore/list when token is invalid. Minimal repro: 

```
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer BADTOKEN' \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/keystore/list?tenant=acme
# response (truncated):
{
  "error": "unauthorized",
  "details": "last_valid_key: key-1234abcd, fallback_key: key-9876wxyz"
}
```

frank (Acme-Sec): also saw intermittent 401s + elevated latency around 2026-03-17T14:10Z, included a tiny log snippet: `keystore: unauthorized request for tenant=acme, resolver returned key id key-1234abcd` — severity: high for compliance team.

tanya (eng-runtime): Thanks — can you paste the exact request id/ts? we need the full trace to see whether the key id is coming from the auth layer or from a downstream cache. Also: is the token being replayed or malformed?

frank (Acme-Sec): request-id `req_0a7c9f` at 2026-03-17T14:10:22Z. They're running an internal scanner that flagged it as CVE-2026-XXXX (public advisory referenced). No public exploit repo that we can see yet but customer is treating as critical.

lee (sec-oncall): Triage acknowledged. Immediate mitigations: 1) disable verbose keystore error details in prod for the affected tenant(s), 2) rotate any keys that may have been exposed, 3) push a hotfix to stop returning key identifiers on 4xx errors. Please confirm reproduction and whether this affects automated backups/audit logs.

maria (sre): I can schedule a canary patch deploy in prod-canary now. Command I'll run: `kubectl -n prod-canary rollout restart deploy/kms-service` then smoke tests against `canary.acme.redwood.example`. If canary looks good I can escalate to a staggered rollout.

tanya (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation we can do immediately (hotpatch): strip `details` fields from error responses at the edge and flip verbose logging to false for keystore path. PR ready: #4321 — small change in auth middleware. ETA: 3.5-4h for canary verification, 18-24h for full rollout if no regressions. Full patch (remove key id material from all error paths + add defensive filtering in cache layer) ETA 24-48h.

ops-billing: Heads-up — customer key rotations + re-encrypt operations may cause billing spikes depending on key counts. If we trigger mass rotations, finance wants a heads-up so we can credit for any abnormal charges.

jordan (support): I'll draft customer-facing note. Confirm: canary deploy window and a conservative global rollout ETA. We should also offer to rotate Acme keys for them if they want us to handle it.

lee (sec-oncall): Draft for customer (short): "We acknowledge CVE-2026-XXXX affecting keystore error detail leakage. Immediate action: we are rolling a hotpatch to remove key identifiers from error responses (canary in ~4h). We will rotate any exposed keys on request and can perform those rotations for you under a high-priority customer ops runbook. Full rollout expected within 24 hours, with post-deploy verification and audit of logs. We will share rotation ETA for affected keys within 2 hours." Please review.

jordan (support): sending now, will CC compliance and ops. Frank — are you OK with canary-first approach?

frank (Acme-Sec): OK canary-first. Please CC our compliance lead (compliance@acme.example). We need rotation within 12 hours ideally. We'll accept a canary as proof.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: kms-service:deploy:canary -> queued at 1803550000. Notified: @maria @tanya.

maria (sre): I'll monitor canary logs and health checks. If `5xx` > 1% or latency p50 increases > 50ms we will abort and rollback. Rolling smoke tests now.

tanya (eng-runtime): I'll cut the hotpatch PR to staging and attach the minimal repro test to CI so we don't regress. Repro in CI: 
```
# simplified test
resp = client.get('/v1/keystore/list', token='bad')
assert 'details' not in resp.json()
```
If green, request manual approve for prod-canary.

jordan (support): Thanks all — I'll keep the thread updated and call out when the customer rotation request comes in.

frank (Acme-Sec): Thanks team. Please mark this as P0 and include timestamped audit of who had access to keys in last 30 days. We need that for our regulator.

lee (sec-oncall): Copy — security will pull audit logs and provide a signed statement after rotation completes. Action items assigned: @tanya hotpatch PR, @maria canary deploy & monitor, @jordan customer comms, @ops-billing finance notification.
